question.worked_solution:
$$
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2{x}^{3}-2x-1}{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2{x}^{3}-2x}{{x}^{2}-1}-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2{x}^{3}-2x}{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x({x}^{2}-1)}{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}+\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
